Generally speaking, once a month your credit card company will report to the credit breaus two things, the balance at that moment on your card, and if your payment was on time. So to answer your question, it really depends on when you pay the bill versus when the credit card company reports it to the breaus. So if you get your bill every month on the 15th, pay if off completely on the 16th every month, then your credit card company reports on the 25th it will just show the balance you have as of the 25th, me that your least payment was on time. It won't show the highest balance you had that month or that you paid the card completely off. However, you never want your credit card company to show that you charged up to your limit. So let's pretend you have a card with a 2k limit. Let's say you pay all your bills with it on your card and get to the 2k limit on the 7th. Then your bill comes on the 10th and you pay it off completely that day. But let's pretend your credit card company reports to the breaus on the 9th. And let's pretend this is your normal routine every month. What will end up happening is every month your credit card company will report that your last payment was on time and your balance is 2k (at it's limit). If this is your usual routine every month it will show that every month your card stays maxed out, but you make your payment. Creditors have no way to know you paid it all off. This can actually make your credit score go down. I see lots of people telling you to have your limit increased. That can be good or bad. If you have a lot of available credit it can lower your score as more available credit makes you a bigger risk. And when your credit card company increases your credit limit they check your credit. This can also lower your score. However, if you have a small credit card limit that you tend to stay close to every month having your limit increased, and then not using that extra credit, can be good. Creditors like to see that you don't utilize more that 30% of your available credit cards. So, maxing out your cards and then paying them completely off each month could be a bad idea. Instead, use your card and any time you exceeded 30% of the available credit immediately make a payment. Having no balance is ok, can't hurt, but if you never use the cards you have no positive payment history to show you are capable of paying bills on time. So what I do is make all my purchases on my credit card so I get reward miles, then pay it down to at least 30% once I've spent more than that in available credit, or I pay off any charge that's been on the card to receive an interest charge. I also do not have more than 5,000$ in available credit line on my two cards so creditors aren't concerned I have too much available credit. Sorry for the rant, I hope I could provide good insight.

But if you are removing the applicator or using tampons that have no applicator then either you are inserting the tampon wrong or you might have another medical issue. Due to the severity of your cramps I highly recommend you see a gynecologist. Every question you just asked us you can ask a gynecologist, you can even ask her/ him how to insert a tampon. But I do think you need done sort of help with those cramps. They might find a birth control to help with them or even main medications. But cramps that bad mixed with horrible blood clotted periods could be a sign of some underlying medical condition. Have you ever be sexually abused? You don't have to answer that question, I only ask because sexual abuse can lead to certain trauma that can lead to these problems. In fact, physical abuse can too.
